Categorical (multinomial) models in table_regression()

Source: R/table_regression_categorical.R
table_regression_categorical.Rd

table_regression() reads the baseline-category logit models of nnet::multinom() and the discrete-choice models of mlogit::mlogit(). A single multinom fit sets predictors as rows and one column group per non-reference outcome category, so the effect of a predictor can be compared across equations along its row. An mlogit fit renders per-alternative rows in two segments: the alternative-invariant coefficients, then one section per non-reference alternative. Under exponentiate = TRUE both give odds ratios against the reference outcome or alternative.

Usage

table_regression(
  models,
  exponentiate = FALSE,
  show_columns = NULL,
  outcome_labels = NULL,
  ...  # the arguments of every class: see ?table_regression
)

This family has no argument of its own. The other arguments are documented in table_regression(); the values they take for categorical models are listed below.

Engines

ClassEngineAMEExponentiateBlocksvcov
multinomnnet::multinom()per outcomeORper-outcome blocksclassical, CR1
mlogitmlogit::mlogit()noORper-alternative rowsclassical, CR1

AME: whether the average-marginal-effects columns are available; per outcome is one effect per outcome category. Exponentiate: what exponentiate = TRUE gives. Blocks: how the class lays out its coefficient rows. vcov: the values of vcov the class accepts. The same rows are returned by subset(table_regression_models(), family == "Categorical").

What the table shows

A single multinom model. Predictors as rows, one column group per non-reference outcome category (spanner = category name). The note Reference outcome: <level>. names the base category (Stata's "base outcome" line), and outcome_labels relabels the spanners (e.g. "Student vs Employed"). The fit statistics print once, under the first group. When per-category AMEs are requested, the reference category appears as a last, AME-only group: its coefficient cells are empty, since the reference has no equation, and its AMEs complete the zero sum across categories. The default show_columns compacts to B, SE and p as for several models; request atomic tokens to restore the intervals.

Several multinom models, or nested = TRUE. One row per (category, predictor) pair: categories within models would need two spanner levels. tidy() and output = "long" always return the long form ("<category>: <term>" rows), whatever the display; as_structured() and output = "data.frame" follow the displayed table (one column set per category), as they do for every other layout.

An mlogit model. Two segments, the presentation of Stata's asclogit. The Alternative-invariant section holds the coefficients of the alternative attributes, one row each, shared across alternatives. Then one section per non-reference alternative collects its intercept and its case-specific coefficients, each against the reference that the note names (Reference alternative: <level>.). The n row counts choice situations, not the rows of the long-format data.

Fit statistics. See Fit statistics below.

Values of the shared arguments

exponentiate

Odds ratios of each outcome against the reference outcome: the baseline-category logits are log-odds (Agresti 2002; SAS prints "Odds Ratio Estimates" under its generalized-logit link; Stata's mlogit, rrr labels the same quantity a relative-risk ratio).

show_columns

The AME tokens give one effect per outcome category for multinom. They are refused for mlogit: marginaleffects computes predictions but not slopes for its one-row-per-choice data structure.

outcome_labels

For a single multinom model, the labels of the category spanners: one per non-reference outcome category, unique, in model order. The AME-only group of the reference category, when shown, keeps its own name, and FALSE changes nothing, as there is no Outcome row to remove.

model_labels

Refused for a single multinomial model: its column groups are outcome categories, relabeled by outcome_labels.

vcov, cluster

"classical" and "CR1" for both classes. cluster has one entry per observation for multinom and one per choice situation for mlogit. See Standard errors, degrees of freedom and intervals.

nested

TRUE compares nested multinom fits by likelihood-ratio test, the convention of anova.multinom().

ci_method

"wald" only.

standardized

Refused.

Standard errors, degrees of freedom and intervals

The coefficients are tested by Wald z. Cluster-robust "CR1" comes from sandwich::vcovCL(): the CR0 sandwich scaled by \(G/(G-1)\), G the number of clusters. For multinom it needs sandwich >= 3.1-2, which added its estfun() method, and the AME columns follow it. Under "CR1", a nested hierarchy is tested by the Wald chi-square of the added coefficients on the robust matrix.

Fit statistics

A multinom fit defaults to c("nobs", "pseudo_r2_mcfadden", "aic"), an mlogit fit to c("nobs", "aic"), its n counting choice situations. See R-squared of glm and categorical models in table_regression().

What is refused, and why

  • HC* for multinom: a multi-equation model has no working residuals or hat values, so the HC meat cannot be formed.

  • HC* for mlogit: sandwich::vcovHC() computes a result for it but mis-scales the meat for its per-chooser score structure.

  • "CR0", "CR2", "CR3", "bootstrap" and "jackknife": "CR1" is the one robust estimator of these classes.

  • The AME columns for mlogit (see show_columns above).

  • model_labels for a single multinom model, ci_method = "profile" and standardized.

References

Agresti, A. (2002). Categorical data analysis (2nd ed.). Wiley. doi:10.1002/0471249688

See also

table_regression() for the arguments shared by all classes; table_regression_models() for the registry of supported classes and the other families; the Multinomial regression tables article.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("nnet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- nnet::multinom(employment_status ~ age + sex,
                        data = sochealth, trace = FALSE)
  print(table_regression(fit, exponentiate = TRUE))
}
